manualChecklist.instruction: With US14 Scale Hero selected in the installed editor, use real mouse input to request Auto, GPU Visual, Hybrid Authoritative, and CPU Deterministic/Fallback through the Animator controls. Inspect the effective mode, fallback reason, batching granularity, publication generations, transfers, readbacks, waits, and bounded mode-switch history in Animation Diagnostics, then restore Auto without collecting timing measurements under the active power limit.

Use real mouse input to hide and show US14 Scale Hero repeatedly, reimport the valid source, and inspect Scene View, Game View, and the authored camera after each transition. Confirm no bind flash, mixed generation, stale deformation, or partial asset publication; leave the valid source, visible object, Auto policy, and stopped editor state restored.

Use real keyboard input to review the malformed-reload preservation evidence and canceled-before-commit transaction, then repeat one supported cancellation through the installed animation job UI. Confirm the last-known-good generated package and authored object name remain unchanged and that no canceled work publishes after the protected boundary.

Use only a documented supported installed-editor renderer-loss or recovery procedure, together with the renderer-independent safe-save command and Animation Diagnostics, to verify a usable prior or conservative fallback state and no stale GPU ownership. Do not invent an MCP fault injector or unsafe OS/device action; if no supported procedure is available, do not complete this checklist item and leave T134 open. Do not run performance regression measurements under the active power limit.

Using real mouse input in the installed editor, inspect the advertised animation capability descriptors, request and result schemas, declared limits, generation contracts, mutability, approval policies, and durable-job behavior. Cross-check the scripted asset import/reimport/inspect, controller edit/validation, advanced authoring, preview, runtime parameter, procedural, retarget, motion-match, ragdoll, recording, diagnostics, residency, profiler, camera, and job get/cancel evidence against the corresponding editor windows. Deliberately approve the exact high-impact animation import, reimport, motion-database build, recording start, and recording stop requests, and retain the approval UI receipts and native-window screenshots. Do not use project create/open/close/switch or application lifecycle operations.

Using real keyboard input, verify the scripted exact retry replays one receipt, the changed-payload retry conflicts without publication, the dry-run leaves authored bytes unchanged, and the stale-generation request rejects atomically. While the durable animation import, reimport, motion-database build, successful recording, and canceled recording jobs remain retained, disconnect and reconnect MCP, rediscover the same required animation tool inventory, poll the original job IDs and correlated diagnostics from the new connection, and verify the cancellation result remains unpublished. Exercise Play Mode and Scene/Game/custom-camera review, then exit and prove authored scene state restores while the two explicitly declared recording output files remain as the only allowed Play Mode project additions. Performance timing is intentionally deferred because the power-limited host cannot produce comparable regression measurements.
